title: arXiv Physics — Daily notable papers (11 November 2026)
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this inferred ordering uses sparse attention and scientific signals. Citation evidence is limited for papers only just announced, so this is a notable-recent-paper ranking, not a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
sections.abstract: A 63-qubit superconducting processor simulates string evolution in a two-spatial-dimensional Z₂ gauge theory, resolving charge and flux spreading, pair creation, and transverse rearrangement across confined and deconfined regimes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report rapid charge/flux spreading in the deconfined regime, enhanced matter occupation near pair-creation resonance, and suppressed spreading at strong electric fields.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; digital quantum simulation of a (2+1)D Z₂ lattice gauge theory on 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas
sections.unique_caveat: The implementation is a finite 5×4 matter lattice and measures circuits up to 15 second-order Trotter steps; noise rescaling and symmetry checks are part of the analysis, so the result does not establish scalable quantum advantage.
sections.ranking_evidence: An independent Quantum Zeitgeist report dated 11 November covered the 63-qubit experiment; the paper also reports direct Gauss-law checks and string-path measurements, making it a concrete hardware result rather than a proposal.

sections.title: Search for heavy top quark partners with charge 5/3 in the single-lepton final state in proton-proton collisions at √s = 13 TeV
sections.abstract: CMS searches 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton collisions for pair-produced charge-5/3 top partners in conventional top–W and exotic top–charged-Higgs decay modes, finding no excess and setting 95% confidence-level mass limits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors exclude masses up to 1.63 TeV for the top–W mode and up to 1.74 TeV for the top–charged-Higgs mode when the charged Higgs mass is 800 GeV; they report no significant excess.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; CMS proton-proton collision data at √s = 13 TeV collected in 2016–2018, analyzed in a single-electron or single-muon final state
sections.unique_caveat: The quoted exclusions assume exclusive branching to the specified decay chain and cover the single-lepton channel; the exotic interpretation is limited to simulated mass points satisfying its kinematic threshold.
sections.ranking_evidence: The arXiv record says the work was submitted to Physical Review D; the analysis uses the full 2016–2018 CMS 138 fb⁻¹ sample and reports the first limits for the top-partner-to-top-plus-charged-Higgs mode.

sections.title: Constraints on Lorentz Invariance Violation from PeV Gamma Rays of Cygnus X-3 Observed by LHAASO
sections.abstract: Using LHAASO observations of photons up to 3.7 PeV from Cygnus X-3, the authors find no predicted high-energy cutoff and derive stronger lower limits on energy scales for superluminal Lorentz-invariance violation.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a second-order LIV energy scale above roughly 10⁻² of the Planck scale in the photon-splitting channel; this is a constraint, not a detection of Lorentz violation.
sections.evidence_type: observational; analysis of LHAASO KM2A data from four Cygnus X-3 flaring periods (2019–2024), totaling 692.8 days, with source-spectrum and cutoff models
sections.unique_caveat: The intrinsic source spectrum is the dominant systematic: the authors estimate about a 9.5% effect on the cutoff limit when changing spectral model; the result also tests specified superluminal LIV scenarios.
sections.ranking_evidence: It is cross-listed across astrophysics and phenomenology and converts multi-PeV photons in a measured LHAASO dataset into a quantitative constraint, reporting an improvement of nearly an order of magnitude over prior limits.

sections.title: Observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between two atoms
sections.abstract: The authors confine dysprosium atom pairs to densities above 10¹⁶ cm⁻³ and observe coherent near-field dipole interactions, large momentum transfer after single-photon emission, and a dipole-induced two-body resonance shift.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report single-photon momentum transfer of order 10ℏk, coherent light-induced dipole forces, and a two-body Lamb shift dominated by near-field interactions.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ¹⁶²Dy atom pairs in a three-dimensional optical lattice, probed through momentum distributions, light scattering, fluorescence spectra, and atom loss
sections.unique_caveat: The study is limited to optical transitions and atom pairs; the authors note that detuning-asymmetric photoassociative loss may involve motional dynamics and complex excited-state potentials.
sections.ranking_evidence: The work combines a direct laboratory observation with a measurement regime above nλ̄³ = 10, over an order of magnitude beyond the cited earlier cold-atom regime, and is cross-listed in atomic and quantum physics.

sections.title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum
sections.abstract: Four physical-pion-mass, Nf = 2+1+1 twisted-mass lattice-QCD ensembles at four lattice spacings are used to extrapolate the light, strange, and charm nucleon sigma terms to the continuum.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain σπN = 53.0(7.4)(1.6) MeV, σs = 58.2(17.0)(2.1) MeV, and σc = 112(28)(25) MeV, with statistical and systematic uncertainties listed in that order.
sections.evidence_type: computational; global fits to four Nf = 2+1+1 twisted-mass lattice-QCD ensembles at physical pion masses and lattice spacings from 0.080 to 0.049 fm
sections.unique_caveat: The quoted strange- and charm-term uncertainties remain sizable, and the continuum values depend on global fits across a finite set of ensembles despite the authors’ treatment of excited-state contamination.
sections.ranking_evidence: The result is cross-listed in four physics archives and combines physical-pion-mass ensembles with an explicit continuum extrapolation; the paper reports separate statistical and systematic errors for all three sigma terms.
